rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends Moses to Pharaoh, Egypt's king from whom he fled, to call him to worship God alone and treat the Israelites well; Pharaoh transgressed, preferred worldly life, and forgot God.
rows.anchor: أي: اذهب إلى فرعون ملك مصر، الذي خرجت فارا منه وهاربا، فادعه إلى عبادة الله وحده لا شريك له

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb's divine address assures Moses of God's protection, portrays Pharaoh as arrogant despite long respite and abundant provision, orders a gentle summons to monotheism and warning, forbids fear or envy of worldly display, and promises lasting honor for God's friends.
rows.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه: قال الله لموسى: انطلق برسالتي فإنك بعيني وسمعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's signs here mean His proofs, demonstrations, and miracles.
rows.anchor: أي: بحججي وبراهيني ومعجزاتي

rows.speaker: علي ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ali ibn Abi Talha, glosses the command as: do not delay.
rows.anchor: قال علي ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس: لا تبطئا

rows.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Mujahid, reporting from Ibn Abbas, glosses it as: do not weaken.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد، عن ابن عباس: لا تضعفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Aaron must persist in remembering God while facing Pharaoh; remembrance strengthens them and overcomes him, as a hadith describes the servant who remembers God while confronting his opponent.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنهما لا يفتران في ذكر الله، بل يذكران الله في حال مواجهة فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh rebelled, became arrogantly defiant toward God, and disobeyed Him.
rows.anchor: أي: تمرد وعتا وتجهرم على الله وعصاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is a profound lesson: although Pharaoh was supremely arrogant and Moses God's chosen servant, Moses and Aaron were commanded to address him gently.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية فيها عبرة عظيمة، وهو أن فرعون في غاية العتو والاستكبار

rows.speaker: يزيد الرقاشي
rows.claim: Yazid al-Raqqashi remarks that God endears Himself to one who opposes Him, so how much more to one who accepts and calls upon Him.
rows.anchor: كما قال يزيد الرقاشي عند قوله: {فقولا له قولا لينا} : يا من يتحبب إلى من يعاديه

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says the gentle words tell Pharaoh that God is nearer to pardon and forgiveness than to anger and punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: قولا له: إني إلى العفو والمغفرة أقرب مني إلى الغضب والعقوبة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima identifies the gentle utterance as the testimony that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة في قوله: {فقولا له قولا لينا} قال: لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد عن الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Amr ibn Ubayd reports Hasan al-Basri's view: excuse Pharaoh by telling him he has a Lord and a return, with Paradise and Hell ahead.
rows.anchor: عمرو بن عبيد، عن الحسن البصري: {فقولا له قولا لينا} أعذرا إليه

rows.speaker: علي عن الضحاك
rows.claim: Ali's transmitted gloss is “كنه”; Sufyan al-Thawri likewise reportedly glossed it “كنه بأبي مرة.”
rows.anchor: وقال بقية، عن علي بن هارون، عن رجل، عن الضحاك بن مزاحم، عن النزال بن سبرة، عن علي في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir concludes that their invitation should use soft, gentle, accessible words, which better reach hearts and prove more effective; he connects this to the command to invite with wisdom and good counsel.
rows.anchor: والحاصل من أقوالهم أن دعوتهما له تكون بكلام رقيق لين قريب سهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance means turning back from what is forbidden, while fear means attaining obedience; the wording echoes the description of one who seeks to remember or fear God.
rows.anchor: فالتذكر: الرجوع عن المحذور، والخشية: تحصيل الطاعة

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan says Moses and Aaron should not demand Pharaoh's destruction before they have first given him an excuse and warning.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري [في قوله] (3) {لعله يتذكر أو يخشى}

rows.speaker: زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل، ويروى لأمية بن أبي الصلت
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a poem attributed to Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, also attributed to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt by Ibn Ishaq, depicting Moses and Aaron calling Pharaoh to God and asking who made the heavens, light, sun, and vegetation.
rows.anchor: وهاهنا نذكر شعر زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل، ويروى لأمية بن أبي الصلت فيما ذكره ابن إسحاق

words: إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Aaron sought God's protection, fearing Pharaoh might hasten to punish them or attack them unjustly.
rows.anchor: يعنيان أن يبدر إليهما بعقوبة، أو يعتدي عليهما فيعاقبهما وهما لا يستحقان منه ذلك

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd glosses “يَفْرُط” as “he hastens.”
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: {أن يفرط} يعجل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains “يَفْرُط” as Pharaoh extending his violence against them.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يبسط علينا

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak, reporting from Ibn Abbas, glosses “يَطْغى” as transgressing.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: {أو أن يطغى} : يعتدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears both sides and sees where they are; nothing is hidden from Him. Pharaoh's forelock is under God's control, and Pharaoh cannot speak, breathe, or strike except by permission; God protects, helps, and supports Moses and Aaron.
rows.anchor: أي: لا تخافا منه، فإنني معكما أسمع كلامكما وكلامه، وأرى مكانكما ومكانه

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah reports that when God sent Moses to Pharaoh, Moses asked what to say; God told him “هيا شراهيا,” which al-A'mash glossed as the Living before and after everything. Ibn Kathir calls the chain good and the report unusual.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن مرة، عن أبي عبيدة، عن عبد الله قال: لما بعث الله عز وجل موسى إلى فرعون قال: رب، أي شيء أقول؟

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas's hadith of al-Futun, Moses and Aaron waited at Pharaoh's door for a time without permission, then were admitted after a severe barrier was lifted.
rows.anchor: قد تقدم في حديث "الفتون" عن ابن عباس أنه قال: مكثا

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the brothers waited at the palace for two years, with no one daring to inform Pharaoh, until a court entertainer told him; Pharaoh summoned them, and Moses identified himself as a messenger whom Pharaoh recognized.
rows.anchor: وذكر محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار: أن موسى وأخاه هارون خرجا، فوقفا بباب فرعون يلتمسان الإذن

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi relates that Moses reunited with his mother and brother, enlisted Aaron to help summon Pharaoh, and they went by night; after Moses knocked with his staff, guards called him mad, but Pharaoh ordered them in.
rows.anchor: وذكر السدي أنه لما قدم بلاد مصر، ضاف أمه وأخاه وهما لا يعرفانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “sign” is a proof and miracle from God; “peace upon whoever follows guidance” means peace to Pharaoh if he follows guidance.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {قد جئناك بآية من ربك} أي: بدلالة ومعجزة من ربك، {والسلام على من اتبع الهدى} أي: والسلام عليك إن اتبعت الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet opened his letter to Heraclius with the same greeting, then invited him to Islam and promised safety and a doubled reward from God.
rows.anchor: ولهذا لما كتب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى هرقل عظيم الروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musaylimah claimed partnership in prophethood and divided the land and its people between them; Muhammad answered him with the same greeting and God's promise to grant the land to whichever servants He wills.
rows.anchor: وكذلك لما كتب مسيلمة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كتابا صورته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation confines punishment to whoever denies God's signs and turns away from obedience: denial is inward, while turning away is action. Ibn Kathir links this to several warnings of punishment.
rows.anchor: أي: قد أخبرنا الله فيما أوحاه إلينا من الوحي المعصوم أن العذاب متحمض لمن كذب بآيات الله

words: ولقد أريناه آياتنا كلها فكذب وأبى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The referent is Pharaoh: proofs and signs were established before him and plainly witnessed, yet he rejected them in disbelief, stubbornness, and transgression, as others rejected signs despite inward certainty.
rows.anchor: يعني: فرعون، أنه قامت عليه الحجج والآيات والدلالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses feared that people would be deceived by the sorcerers before he threw his staff.
rows.anchor: أي خاف على الناس أن يفتتنوا بسحرهم ويغتروا بهم قبل أن يلقي ما في يمينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God immediately inspired Moses to throw what was in his right hand, namely his staff.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله تعالى إليه في الساعة الراهنة أن {وألق ما في يمينك} يعني: عصاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff became a huge, terrifying serpent with eyes, limbs, neck, head, and fangs; it pursued and swallowed every rope and stick before the crowd in broad daylight.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنها صارت تنينا (4) عظيما هائلا

words: إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The public miracle made the proof clear and nullified the sorcerers' work: what they devised was a magician's scheme, and a magician never succeeds wherever he comes.
rows.anchor: فقامت المعجزة، واتضح البرهان، وبطل ما كانوا يعملون

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reportedly ordered that a sorcerer be killed when caught and recited this verse; al-Tirmidhi transmitted the report's basis both as a Companion statement and as Prophetic, with no grading given here.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، عن جندب بن عبد الله البجلي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "إذا أخذتم -يعني الساحر-فاقتلوه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Experienced sorcerers knew Moses's feat was neither magic nor trickery but undeniable truth, possible only for the Creator who says “Be,” and they prostrated and believed in the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: علموا علم اليقين أن هذا الذي فعله موسى ليس من قبيل السحر والحيل، وأنه حق لا مرية فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ubayd ibn Umayr say the sorcerers began the day as sorcerers and ended it as righteous martyrs.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال ابن عباس، وعبيد بن عمير:كانوا أول النهار سحرة، وفي آخر النهار شهداء بررة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b estimates that the sorcerers numbered eighty thousand.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب: كانوا ثمانين ألفا

rows.speaker: القاسم بن أبي بزة
rows.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza estimates that they numbered seventy thousand.
rows.anchor: وقال القاسم بن أبي بزة: كانوا سبعين ألفا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi estimates that they numbered a little over thirty thousand.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: بضعة وثلاثين ألفا

rows.speaker: الثوري عن عبد العزيز بن رفيع عن أبي ثمامة
rows.claim: Al-Thawri, transmitting through Abd al-Aziz ibn Rafi from Abu Thumama, gives the number as nineteen thousand.
rows.anchor: وقال الثوري: عن عبد العزيز بن رفيع، عن أبي ثمامة: كان (2) سحرة فرعون تسعة عشر ألفا

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq says they numbered fifteen thousand.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: كانوا خمسة عشر ألفا

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says they numbered twelve thousand.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار كانوا اثني عشر ألفا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: An Ibn Abbas report transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim says seventy men who began as sorcerers ended the day as martyrs.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس قال: كانت السحرة سبعين رجلا أصبحوا سحرة وأمسوا شهداء

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Awza'i says that when the sorcerers fell prostrate, Paradise was raised for them until they saw it.
rows.anchor: قال الأوزاعي: لما خر السحرة سجدا رفعت لهم الجنة حتى نظروا إليها

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says they saw their abodes being built for them while they prostrated.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله: {فألقي السحرة سجدا} قال: رأوا منازلهم

rows.speaker: عكرمة والقاسم بن أبي بزة
rows.claim: Ikrima and al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza give the same account that the sorcerers saw their abodes being built as they prostrated.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال عكرمة والقاسم بن أبي بزة

words: آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After witnessing the miracle and his own sorcerers publicly convert despite their defeat, Pharaoh defiantly falsifies the truth and abuses his power to threaten them.
rows.anchor: حين رأى ما رأى من المعجزة الباهرة والآية العظيمة، ورأى الذين قد استنصر بهم قد آمنوا

words: آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's “you believed him” means you affirmed Moses; “before I gave you permission” accuses them of acting without his order and against him.
rows.anchor: وقال {آمنتم له} أي: صدقتموه {قبل أن آذن لكم} أي: وما أمرتكم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh knowingly lies that Moses taught the sorcerers magic and that they colluded with him to deceive Pharaoh and his subjects; he makes the same accusation elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقال قولا يعلم هو والسحرة والخلق كلهم أنه بهت وكذب: {إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر}

words: فلأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh threatens to mutilate and kill them, then crucify them publicly as an example.
rows.anchor: أي: لأجعلنكم مثلة [ولأقتلنكم] (4) ولأشهرنكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh was the first to carry out this form of punishment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فكان أول من فعل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh says they claim he and his people are astray while Moses and his followers are guided, and threatens that they will learn who suffers the harsher, longer-lasting punishment.
rows.anchor: أي أنتم تقولون: إني وقومي على ضلالة، وأنتم مع موسى وقومه على الهدى

words: لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorcerers' lives became negligible to them for God; they refuse to choose Pharaoh over the guidance and certainty they have received.
rows.anchor: فلما صال عليهم بذلك وتوعدهم، هانت عليهم أنفسهم في الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “by the One who originated us” can either be an oath or be grammatically coordinated with “the proofs.”
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون قسما، ويحتمل أن يكون معطوفا على البينات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will not prefer Pharaoh to their Creator, who brought them from nothing and first formed them from clay; He alone deserves worship and submission.
rows.anchor: لا (5) نختارك على فاطرنا وخالقنا الذي أنشأنا من العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do whatever he wishes and whatever lies within his power.
rows.anchor: أي: فافعل ما شئت وما وصلت إليه يدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's authority reaches only this transient life; the sorcerers desire the everlasting abode.
rows.anchor: أي: إنما لك تسلط في هذه الدار، وهي دار الزوال ونحن قد رغبنا في دار القرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On returning and seeing the grave event among his people, Moses became furious, dropped the divine tablets, and seized and dragged Aaron by the head; Ibn Kathir says the fuller account is in al-A'raf and invokes “news is not like seeing.”
rows.anchor: يقول مخبرا عن موسى، عليه السلام، حين رجع إلى قومه، فرأى ما قد حدث فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks why Aaron did not follow him and report their deviation immediately, and whether he disobeyed the prior appointment to remain and reform the people.
rows.anchor: أي: فتخبرني بهذا الأمر أول ما وقع {أفعصيت أمري}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's prior instruction to Aaron was to act as his deputy among the people, reform them, and avoid the way of corrupters.
rows.anchor: وهو قوله: {اخلفني في قومي وأصلح ولا تتبع سبيل المفسدين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Moses and Aaron were full brothers, invoking their mother was gentler and more emotionally affecting.
rows.anchor: مع أنه شقيقه لأبويه؛ لأن ذكر الأم هاهنا أرق وأبلغ، أي: في الحنو والعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron explains that he feared following Moses to report the crisis would prompt Moses to accuse him of leaving the Israelites divided and alone.
rows.anchor: هذا اعتذار من هارون عند موسى في سبب تأخره عنه، حيث لم يلحقه فيخبره بما كان من هذا الخطب الجسيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You did not heed my word” means Aaron would have failed to observe Moses's instruction when entrusted with the people.
rows.anchor: أي: وما راعيت ما أمرتك به حيث استخلفتك فيهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Aaron stood in awe of Moses and was obedient to him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وكان هارون هائبا له مطيعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir recalls the hadith “news is not like direct seeing” to frame Moses's response on witnessing the event himself.
rows.anchor: وذكرنا هناك حديث "ليس الخبر كالمعاينة"

words: ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must not gaze at the affluent and their blessings: they are a fading flower and passing pleasure given as a test, and few servants give thanks.
rows.anchor: لا تنظر إلى هؤلاء المترفين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses “groups among them” as the wealthy; God has given the Prophet better, as also stated in the linked passage about the seven oft-repeated verses and Quran.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {أزواجا منهم} يعني: الأغنياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife reward God has stored for His Messenger is immense beyond description; the promise that his Lord will give until he is content confirms that God's provision is better and more lasting.
rows.anchor: ما ادخره الله تعالى لرسوله في الدار الآخرة أمر عظيم لا يحد ولا يوصف

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In an account in Sahih, Umar saw the Prophet lying on a coarse mat with little in the room and wept at the contrast with Khosrow and Caesar; the Prophet replied that their good things were hastened for them in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيح: أن عمر بن الخطاب لما دخل علي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في تلك المشربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite being able to possess wealth, the Prophet was the most ascetic: he distributed what came to him among God's servants and saved nothing for the next day.
rows.anchor: أزهد الناس في الدنيا مع القدرة عليها، إذا حصلت له ينفقها هكذا وهكذا، في عباد الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Abu Sa'id says the Prophet feared most what God might open of worldly bloom; he defined that bloom as the earth's blessings.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إن أخوف ما أخاف عليكم

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi interpret the flower of worldly life as its adornment.
rows.anchor: قتادة والسدي: زهرة الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as “so that We may test them in it.”
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة {لنفتنهم فيه} لنبتليهم
